newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Q4 '96 GDP up about 9 pct - Fernandez.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Q4 '96 GDP up about 9 pct - Fernandez.

text.p: Argentina's economy expanded around nine percent in the last quarter of 1996, resulting in gross domestic product growth of around four percent for the whole year, Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said Thursday.

"All the ... indicators we are observing today are suggesting that we may be getting about nine percent growth in the fourth quarter," Fernandez told Reuters Financial Television in an interview conducted in Paris.
"And that would imply that for the whole of 1996 we may be close to four percent," he added.
Fernandez, who was in Paris participating in an economic panel before flying on to Davos, Switzerland, for a World Economic Forum meeting, also forecast GDP could grow more than five percent in 1997.
"If everything continues in the way we are looking at at the present time, that could be a very conservative estimate, five percent," the minister said.

If the economic recovery consolidates and the government succeeds in reforming labor legislation, unemployment could be reduced by as much as four percentage points from the current 17.3 percent, Fernandez said.
He also dismissed suggestions that Argentina, which is planning to issue a total $8.5 billion in bonds this year, could saturate the markets.
"We don't expect any trouble at all. Of course, we will continue to monitor market conditions," said Fernandez.
He added the country would be "very active" in the market with peso-denominated bonds, provided the conditions are right.
On Wednesday he announced in Switzerland the launching of a 10-year, 500 million peso Eurobond.
